correctness.rationale: The cut hyperplanes are pairwise disjoint inside the cube because selected vertices have Hamming distance at least two and all depths are below one. The new vertices are exactly the edge-cut points. Surviving cube vertices retain pairwise disjoint illumination orthants, forcing at least \(2^n-|T|\) directions. For each new cut vertex, the direction indexed by its neighboring surviving cube vertex strictly decreases every active facet inequality, including the cut inequality by \(-(n-2)<0\). This yields the matching upper bound. The Banach--Mazur estimate follows from an exact concentric cube sandwich.

value.rationale: The primary source explicitly emphasizes the discontinuity of illumination near the cube while establishing only the first strict drop from \(2^n\). The new theorem determines an exponentially large exact spectrum in every dimension: every integer from \(2^{n-1}\) through \(2^n\) occurs arbitrarily close to the cube. The graph-theoretic independent-set mechanism explains why each selected corner removes exactly one necessary direction while preserving an illuminating neighbor for every new vertex. This is a natural structural refinement of the local-maximizer phenomenon.
